answer: Identity River requires new participants to publicly commit a unique signal—like a geohash of their hardware plus a timestamp—to join. Once registered, identities must periodically sign challenges tied to their original signal location; failure reveals duplicates. Attackers face escalating costs as each attempt exposes prior registrations across geographic regions, turning sybil creation into a meadow of self-incriminating footprints. The fable becomes literal: duplication broadcasts its own evidence.
